selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main warning given at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: Not every reader will understand all of the book, but each reader can still gain some benefit from it.

questions.question: What can a reader learn about fairness from the garden example?
questions.answer: One book can serve people with different abilities, not just one kind of person.

questions.question: How many reasons are given for why the book is hard to understand?
questions.answer: Five reasons are given.

questions.question: Why might that first cause create a challenge for readers?
questions.answer: Readers may not think in the same way the writer does.

questions.question: What is special about the teaching described in the second reason?
questions.answer: It explains belief in Allah’s oneness in a very complete and far-reaching way.

questions.question: According to the third cause, why is a short style not always possible?
questions.answer: Because shortening too much might damage a large truth or leave out needed groundwork.

questions.question: According to the fourth reason, why might the discussion feel too long to some readers?
questions.answer: It includes many different proofs and signs for the same point, which can make the explanation lengthy.

questions.question: What time of year is connected with the inspiration of the treatise in the fifth cause?
questions.answer: Ramadan is connected with it.

questions.question: Why was the first draft not revised in the fifth reason?
questions.answer: The writer felt he was not writing by his own choice, so he thought it was not fitting to change it by his own ideas later.

questions.question: Why did the writer avoid correcting the draft afterward?
questions.answer: He believed the writing did not come simply from his own personal choice, so changing it by his own thoughts seemed wrong.

questions.question: What comfort is given to readers who cannot understand everything in the book?
questions.answer: They are told that they will still receive a share of benefit.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens when a person enters the “garden”?
questions.answer: The person can reach some of the good things there, even if not all of them.

questions.question: What can we infer about the readers from the garden picture?
questions.answer: Readers have different levels of understanding, and that is normal.

questions.question: What is the heart of the first reason?
questions.answer: The book came from the writer’s own personal understanding and was not adjusted for everyone else.

questions.question: Why does the second cause say the topics are hard to grasp quickly?
questions.answer: Because they deal with a very broad and deep explanation of Allah’s unity.

questions.question: Why does the second reason say some people cannot understand everything right away?
questions.answer: Because the matters are very broad, deep, and sometimes long.

questions.question: What is the problem mentioned in the fourth cause?
questions.answer: Many proofs are given for one matter, and that can feel overwhelming to some readers.

questions.question: What is one effect of having many proofs in the fourth reason?
questions.answer: It can make the discussion feel stretched out.

questions.question: What personal hardships are mentioned in the fifth cause?
questions.answer: The writer was troubled, sick, and wrote in a rushed way.

questions.question: How did the writer view his role while writing?
questions.answer: He felt he was not simply acting by his own will.

questions.question: What promise does the passage make to every reader, even if understanding is incomplete?
questions.answer: Every reader will still receive some benefit.

questions.question: What object is used to compare the treatise to something rich and full?
questions.answer: It is compared to a garden full of fruit.

questions.question: Why is it important that the passage says the book is not only for one kind of reader?
questions.answer: It shows that readers can differ and still each have a place in benefiting from it.

questions.question: What is the first cause that makes the book difficult?
questions.answer: It was written from the writer’s own view and not according to the way other people usually understand things.
